status.en: 150 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 38% fewer than the week before, most of them in Abuja, Lagos and Kaduna.
status.nb: 150 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 38 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Abuja, Lagos og Kaduna.

summary.en: Gunmen in Kaduna killed two people and kidnapped 18, while bandits abducted dozens in multiple raids, and suspected armed herders shot a 14‑year-old girl in Nasarawa. In Benue, four people died and 14 were critically ill after a suspected herbal poisoning, and Southern Kaduna killings led HURIWA to ask the DSS to probe possible political sponsorship. The army rescued 16 abducted individuals in Niger State, troops destroyed terrorist enclaves in Borno and forced insurgents to retreat, and youths at Igbudu market attacked NAFDAC officials in Delta. A video shows Wike claiming to have killed the Obi Kererenke movement ahead of 2027. The conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Våpenbærende menn i Kaduna drepte to personer og kidnappet 18, mens banditter bortførte dusinvis i flere raid, og mistenkte væpnede hyrder skjøt en 14‑år gammel jente i Nasarawa. I Benue døde fire personer og 14 ble kritisk syke etter en mistenkt urtemistanke, og drapene i sørlige Kaduna fikk HURIWA til å be DSS undersøke mulig politisk sponsing. Hæren reddet 16 bortførte personer i Niger State, tropper ødela terrorleirer i Borno og tvang opprørere til å trekke seg tilbake, og ungdom på Igbudu-markedet angrep NAFDAC-embetsmenn i Delta. En video viser Wike som hevder å ha drept Obi Kererenke-bevegelsen før 2027. Konflikten førte til 1 486 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
